fr-2026-21512.passage: The NCUA Board (Board) solicits public comment on a proposal to streamline the methods a federally insured credit union (FICU) may use to provide its members with notice of share insurance coverage. The current regulation is overly prescriptive, mandating that a FICU make available hard copies of certain prescribed materials. While a FICU would still be required to provide notice to members, the proposed rule would defer to the FICU on the method used for such notification. Among other methods, a FICU may elect to provide members with a link to updated online resources that will be maintained on the NCUA website. The Board believes the proposed rule will provide greater flexibility, reduce compliance costs for both NCUA and FICUs, and ensure that members are provided with up-to-date information regarding share insurance coverage.

actions.label: Explain this passage in plain language

claims.text: The National Credit Union Administration's board is asking the public to comment on a proposal.
quotes: solicits public comment on a proposal

claims.text: Federally insured credit unions must tell their members about share insurance coverage. The current rule requires them to have certain printed materials available.
quotes: mandating that a FICU make available hard copies of certain prescribed materials

claims.text: Under the proposal, credit unions would still have to notify members, but each credit union would choose how.
quotes: a FICU would still be required to provide notice to members
would defer to the FICU on the method used for such notification

claims.text: One allowed method would be a link to information the NCUA keeps up to date on its website.
quotes: a link to updated online resources that will be maintained on the NCUA website

claims.text: Because the choice of method would be the credit union's, a credit union could still choose printed materials. The passage doesn't say printed materials would be banned.
quotes: would defer to the FICU on the method used

claims.text: The passage doesn't list the other methods that would be allowed, or say whether any standards would apply to the method a credit union chooses.
